text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident: SEV2 - frontend edge 5xx spike (service: api-gateway) — paging infra-oncall and oncall-engineering
Maya Rivera: seeing a large jump in 502/504s from the edge starting ~10:02 UTC. Error rate ~6% on api/* routes, up from <0.2%.
Maya Rivera: quick snapshot: 10:00->10:06 spike. Graphs: env=edge-us-west, upstream latency up, tail timeouts.
Alice Chen: acked. pulling logs now, attaching quick grep.
Alice Chen: ```
edge-proxy-2026-03-15.log: 10:03:12 GET /v1/embed -> 502 "upstream read timeout"
edge-proxy-2026-03-15.log: 10:03:13 GET /v1/generate -> 502 "no healthy upstream"
edge-proxy-2026-03-15.log: 10:04:01 POST /rpc -> 504 "gateway timeout"
```
Carlos Gomez: I'm seeing bursts of TCP resets from the origin pool (model-pool-2). Connections spike and active conn saturates Nginx worker.
Samir Patel: any customer-facing impact? which routes most affected?
Maya Rivera: highest is /v1/embed and some chat streaming routes. Affected customers: a handful of high-volume tenants saw errors and retried -> increased load.
NOC Bot: Detected elevated 502/504s at 10:02 UTC. Notified oncall.
Maya Rivera: initial hypothesis: origin instances overloaded => proxy returns 502s; possible connection LMDB thrash from kv-cache layer causing increased p99 service time.
Alice Chen: rolling healthcheck shows origin instance count stable, but CPU spike on two hosts and slow socket close times.
Carlos Gomez: mitigation plan proposal: 1) temporarily divert traffic away from the busiest instance backends, 2) enable connection_reuse_timeout tweak on edge, 3) increase max_conns on proxy pool, 4) enable degraded-mode fallback for embed route (serve cached embeddings) for 10m.
Samir Patel: +1 on degradations for embed if it reduces errors. We should notify impacted customers.
Maya Rivera: assigning tasks: Alice -> implement traffic diversion (weight adjustment); Carlos -> prepare and run degraded fallback; Maya -> run live telemetry and confirm p50/p99; infra-oncall -> monitor capacity and consider scale-up.
Alice Chen: running `route weight set` to shift 30% traffic off pool-2 to pool-1 in us-west:

`$ rwt route update --service api-gateway --region us-west --weights pool-1=0.7,pool-2=0.3`

Alice Chen: done. Observing drop in errors from some nodes.
Maya Rivera: p50 improved slightly, p99 still elevated. Errors down to 3.2% overall.
Carlos Gomez: deploying degraded fallback for /v1/embed: switch to cached response path. Patch:

```yaml
routes:
  - path: /v1/embed
    fallback: cache-first
    cache_ttl: 300
```

Carlos Gomez: toggled fallback flag via console feature flag `embed_degraded_mode=true`.
Samir Patel: please add a short customer notice to status page and Slack customer channel.
Maya Rivera: posting to status page: "Investigating elevated 5xx rates affecting embedding and streaming routes in US-WEST. Mitigations in progress."
Maya Rivera: current stats: overall 5xx 3.1%, embed-specific 6.8% -> after fallback embed 5xx down to 1.4% for requests hitting fallback.
Alice Chen: telemetry shows origin pool-2 still noisy — connection resets persist. I'm going to cordon the two problematic hosts and rotate them out of LB.
infra-oncall: temporary cordon scheduled. Running `kubectl cordon node-09 node-11` and `drain` with graceful timeout.
Alice Chen: cordon + drain done for node-09, traffic rebalanced. Node-11 draining now.
Maya Rivera: monitoring: after node-09 drain, p99 latency dropped ~18%, 5xx dropped another 0.8 percentage points.
Carlos Gomez: also added a short-term nginx keepalive tweak:
`keepalive_timeout 10s; keepalive_requests 100;` to reduce stale connection pile-up.
Maya Rivera: good. Are there any config regressions that would cause this post-deploy? Any recent rollouts?
Carlos Gomez: no full rollouts in the last 2 hours. There was a config push yesterday but benign. I see an increase in retries from a particular internal job that runs hourly — that amplified pressure.
Samir Patel: we'll follow up with the product owner to throttle that job. Can someone open a ticket?
Maya Rivera: created ticket #INC-2026-1842: "Investigate internal heavy retry job causing origin pressure". Assigned to Platform Tools.
NOC Bot: Noted. Customer-impact log:
- 12 customers saw increased error rate >1% for >5m
- No full outage, intermittent errors, automatic retries mitigated some traffic
Samir Patel: drafting customer message: "We experienced intermittent 502/504 errors in us-west affecting embeddings and streaming requests between 10:02-10:18 UTC. We have applied fallback and rerouted traffic; errors are now reduced. We continue to remediate root cause and will follow up."
Maya Rivera: timeline so far:
- 10:02 UTC: spike detected
- 10:04 UTC: PD alert and channel opened
- 10:08 UTC: traffic weights adjusted
- 10:12 UTC: degraded fallback enabled for embed
- 10:16 UTC: node-09 drained, p99 improved
- 10:18 UTC: overall errors stabilized to ~0.7%
Carlos Gomez: next steps: continue draining node-11, repro stress test on pool-2 in staging, collect tcpdump from problematic hosts, and implement rate-limiter on internal retry job.
Alice Chen: handing off active mitigation to night oncall at 02:00 UTC. leaving playbook notes in the channel and runbook updated.
Maya Rivera: handoff checklist posted.
Maya Rivera: final note: recommend postmortem focusing on (a) why internal retry job wasn't throttled, (b) why origin pool didn't autoscale sooner, (c) better circuit-breaker thresholds on edge.
Samir Patel: agreed. I'll coordinate customer comms and postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident SEV2 closed for active mitigation at 10:48 UTC — monitoring continue. Please file postmortem within 72 hours.
Maya Rivera: closing channel for active triage. If anything regresses ping @infra-oncall and escalate to oncall-engineering.
